use /lib
from ../project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope

export scope HarnessIntegrationScope:
    concept: {HarnessIntegrationConcept}

concept HarnessIntegrationConcept:
    pitch:
        Uses the one-off version for a coding harness for the selected
        ${ProjectDirectoryScope}. For example, `claude -p`

    shape: {HarnessIntegrationShape}

shape HarnessIntegrationShape:
    description:
        Should always run in auto mode.

        The compiled systemPrompt of a prompt's hidden anchor is appended to
        the harness's own system prompt, for example with
        `--append-system-prompt`.
use /lib

export scope HarnessStream:
    concept: {HarnessStreamConcept}

concept HarnessStreamConcept:
    pitch:
        realtime streaming view of output from the @{HarnessStreamConcept}

    shape: {HarnessStreamShape}

shape HarnessStreamShape:
    description:
        monospace, syntax highlighted if applicable, automatically scrolls to
        most recent output.

    formatting:
        Output is pretty formatted: each JSON event is indented across lines,
        with a blank line between events. Lines that are not JSON are shown as
        they arrived.

    design:
        Just the raw text.  There's no border or decoration around the streaming
        component itself.

    autoScroll:
        It will autosroll when we're already scrolled to the bottom of the
        output.  However, if we're not already scrolled, auto scroll will be
        suspended until we've scrolled back to the bottom.

content.text:
I didn't change anything, because the app already does this. Every prompt you send starts a new context.

- **Tasks and Ask questions:** both go through `harness::send` (`src/prompt_mode.rs:1060` and `:1152`). Each call starts a separate `claude -p` process (`src/harness.rs:70`).
- **No carried-over session:** the command never uses `--continue`, `--resume`, `--session-id` or `--fork-session`, so each run is a new conversation.
- **What the harness receives:** only that prompt's compiled `userPrompt` over stdin, plus its `systemPrompt` through `--append-system-prompt`. Earlier tasks or replies in the message list are never added.

The only thing kept between runs is what the app saves to `.suspense/history` for its own history view. Claude never sees it.

This is a behaviour of the code, not a rule in the spec. The spec says to use "the one-off version" of the harness but doesn't say each send must start fresh. You'd need to add that to `spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi` yourself, since I don't edit the spec. If it's there, a later change can't quietly add `--continue`.

If you meant how I work (each new task you give me should be handled by a fresh subagent), tell me and I'll save that to memory.
